Title: Three teenagers injured after flag hits high-voltage power line during Kedah procession
Article:
ALOR SETAR: Three teenagers were injured after a flag carried during the Tokong Sayur procession allegedly came into contact with a high-voltage power line in Mergong here tonight.
The incident is believed to have occurred about 9pm when thousands of participants were taking part in the procession along the main road in Mergong.
The flag, reportedly held by one of the teenagers, was blown by strong winds during light rain before coming into contact with the power line, causing all three teenagers to fall.
The victims, aged 16 and 17, were taken to Sultanah Bahiyah Hospital (HSB), where they were treated in the red zone.
Mergong Tokong Sayur Association secretary Chah Boon Chuan said the annual procession was being held today, with tonight marking its fourth day.
"We usually hold the procession on the fourth day from 8pm to 11pm.
"I was not at the scene when the incident happened and only learnt about it after being informed by participants," he told reporters outside HSB's Emergency Department tonight.
Boon Chuan said the victims were likely still in school based on their ages.
He said the teenagers were receiving treatment and being monitored by doctors.
"I do not know their condition yet as they are still in the red zone," he said.
Earlier, a video circulated on social media showing the injured teenagers lying on the road while other procession participants came to their aid.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: France accuses Musk of 'online harassment' of Europe leaders
Article:
PARIS: France's foreign minister on Tuesday accused the billionaire tycoon and owner of the X social media platform Elon Musk of "online harassment" of European leaders, as he sounded the alarm over the risks of interference in the French 2027 presidential election.
Jean-Noel Barrot warned that ahead of the April-May election – in which far-right candidate Marine Le Pen has her best ever chance of winning the Elysee – "the enemies of democracy will do everything to destabilise us."
"They exploit our divisions and exploit issues such as immigration, secularism, and the Israeli-Palestinian conflict to stoke hatred and tension," he said at a conference organised by the Paris-based Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD).
He singled out an Israeli company – which he did not identify – that he said had created fake French accounts to post over the Israel-Palestinian conflict.
But Barrot also took aim at the "massive online harassment campaigns by Elon Musk against European leaders, aimed at influencing national debates by exploiting the viral nature of his social network."
With France rocked by several weeks of protests by high school students over their conditions, Barrot complained that some coverage of the demonstrations online had been marked by "hostile narratives originating from Russia and China, as well as Iran and the MAGA community" in reference to the supporters of US President Donald Trump.
Trump had last week written on his Truth Social network that "what's happening in France is nothing less than out of control mass migration."
Musk had then commented to his 241.5 million followers on X: "It's an invasion in slow motion, but an invasion nonetheless. And those who support the invasion are traitors who deserve the fate of all traitors."
Barrot vowed that France would hit back.
"We do not tolerate any foreign interference, from wherever it may come. It is a matter of sovereignty," he said.
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Monday it was "clear" Russia had interfered in the UK's bitter 2016 Brexit referendum that resulted in its exit from the European Union.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Communications Ministry, Global Sumud Movement to produce 'Sumud Protocol' mini-series
Article:
BANGI: The Communications Ministry will collaborate with the Global Sumud Movement to produce a television mini-series on the "Sumud Protocol" to raise public awareness, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
He said the production was among several initiatives through which the government would support the efforts of Sumud Nusantara and the Global Sumud Flotilla (GSF).
Fahmi said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's presence at the Sumud Nusantara Dinner tonight sent a clear signal that Malaysia's support for Palestinian liberation went beyond political rhetoric and diplomatic discussions.
"The prime minister's presence tonight sends a very clear signal that this is not merely political rhetoric, nor just what is discussed at diplomatic tables, but is actually driven through support, patronage and mass movements like the Global Sumud Flotilla (GSF).
"We (the government) also hope that, if there are any plans by Sumud Nusantara and GSF, we are ready to help," he told reporters after attending the dinner, held in conjunction with the 2026 World Sumud Congress here today.
He said Anwar was among world leaders who had been most outspoken in expressing Malaysia's position on the need to liberate Palestine and establish an independent Palestinian state.
Fahmi also congratulated Malaysian Islamic Consultative Council (MAPIM) chief executive officer Datuk Dr Sani Araby Abdul Alim Araby for leading and organising various initiatives, which he described as significant.
He added that he and several other ministers would continue supporting Sumud Nusantara and GSF, including through social media assistance.
"We are ready to help. This includes looking at it from the perspective of social media, so this is among several things that the Communications Ministry itself will assist with," he said.
Also present were Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar and Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama) chief executive officer Datin Paduka Nur-ul Afida Kamaludin.

Title: Youths aged 30 and below rack up RM5.4bil in BNPL transactions
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Young people aged 30 and below recorded 65.9 million buy now, pay later (BNPL) transactions worth RM5.4 billion in the first half of 2026, accounting for 37.9 per cent of total transactions nationwide.
In a written reply published on Parliament's website today, the Finance Ministry said Malaysia recorded 173.9 million BNPL transactions worth RM14.7 billion during the period.
The younger demographic accounted for 36.7 per cent of the total transaction value.
As at June 30, their outstanding BNPL financing stood at RM2.4 billion, while non-performing financing amounted to RM96.8 million, or four per cent of the outstanding balance.
The ministry was responding to a question from Datuk Dr Alias Razak (Kuala Nerus-PN) on measures taken by the Consumer Credit Commission to protect young people from excessive indebtedness through BNPL schemes, including comprehensive assessments of consumers' existing credit commitments.

Title: Asian refiners set to make hay as Mideast exports pick up
Article:
Asian refiners look set to be among the biggest beneficiaries of a sustained recovery in Middle Eastern crude oil exports.
Oil exports from the Middle East have largely returned to pre-war levels as tanker movements through the Strait of Hormuz have increased.
Total crude oil and condensate exports from the region — excluding Iran — averaged 18.11 million tonnes a week last month, according to Kpler, compared with a weekly average of around 18.22 million tonnes during the eight weeks prior to the start of the conflict with Iran at the end of February.
However, Middle Eastern fuel exports remain at less than half of pre-war levels due to damage to regional refineries.
That gap works in favour of those who can fill it. Asia holds around 37 per cent of global refining capacity, according to the Energy Institute, and refiners in India, China, South Korea and Singapore are well placed to capture the value attached to turning crude into petrol, diesel and jet fuel.
The gains are not Asia's alone, as refining margins have climbed in all regions this year because fuel prices have risen more than crude oil costs.
Even so, the recovery in Middle Eastern oil supplies should mean that a larger share of the profits and pricing power attached to those barrels will flow to Asia's refining hubs for as long as the Gulf's own refineries remain impaired.
Before the war, Gulf producers spent years expanding downstream. Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and the United Arab Emirates invested heavily in refining and petrochemical capacity, seeking to capture more value from each barrel and reduce reliance on crude exports alone.
The conflict with Iran has disrupted that strategy. Roughly 20 refineries across the Middle East have been struck since fighting began, taking more than 2.3 million barrels per day (bpd) of refining capacity offline.
Damage assessments have been slow because of continuing tensions, but refineries are among the most complex industrial facilities in the energy sector and are much more difficult to repair than oil wells.
That situation means crude output and exports are likely to recover well before refining capacity does, leaving oil producers in the Middle East to rely on other refiners to process their crude.
Asian refineries have cut utilisation rates notably since the conflict began as crude supplies collapsed and shipping costs surged.
The Middle East supplied around 60 per cent of Asia's crude imports last year, according to Kpler, and the sudden drop in flows from the region prompted refiners across Asia to slash throughput by six million bpd in April, according to the International Energy Agency (IEA).
Refinery output has crept higher since, but there's room for further expansion. Many of Asia's large coastal complexes were built specifically to import crude in bulk and convert it into fuels and petrochemicals for domestic and export markets.
India appears particularly well positioned to benefit.
The country sits less than four days by sea from the Gulf's major export terminals and is close to fuel-hungry markets across South and Southeast Asia that have faced supply disruptions since the conflict began.
China also stands to gain. It possesses the world's largest refining system, with capacity of around 18.8 million bpd.
South Korea and Singapore could benefit from higher utilisation rates and increased export activity.
As more crude is routed through Asian processing hubs, those centres become increasingly important to global fuel security, pricing and trade flows.
The broader significance of recovering Gulf production may ultimately be a shift in where influence is exercised across oil markets.
Just over one-third of global crude oil and condensate exports came from the Americas during the second quarter of this year, according to data from Kpler.
That figure compares with an average of roughly 22 per cent since 2024.
The shift has given the United States and other regional producers greater influence over trade flows, pricing dynamics and energy security discussions.
A sustained return of Middle Eastern crude would alter that balance.
A decade ago, Gulf producers set out to capture more value from every barrel by expanding into refining and fuel exports.
The war has pushed them back down the value chain, at least for now. Until they rebuild what was damaged, much of the value in Gulf crude is likely to be captured further east.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Marriage to Malay does not change foreign spouse's ethnicity, says Saifuddin
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Marriage between a Muslim foreign national and a Malaysian of Malay descent does not change the foreign spouse's ethnicity to Malay, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He said the National Registration Department (NRD) would not change the foreign national's ethnicity based on the marriage, which does not alter the individual's original ethnic background.
In a Facebook post today, Saifuddin said the matter had been clearly explained in his written reply in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday.
However, he said some media reports had used headlines that could cause confusion and mislead the public.
He also shared a copy of the parliamentary question and his full answer to enable the public to refer to the information and understand the issue accurately.
Saifuddin urged the public not to draw conclusions based solely on headlines, but to verify facts and understand the context before sharing information.
"Check the facts, understand the real context, and share accurate information so that we do not become part of the spread of misleading information," he said.
Saifuddin stated in a written reply in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday that the marriage of a Muslim foreign national to a Muslim Malay in the country will not change their original ethnic status.
However, he informed that if a child is born from a legally recognised marriage under Malaysian law between a Muslim foreign national and a Malaysian citizen of Malay descent, the child's mother or father can choose whether the child is registered according to the mother's or father's ethnicity.
Saifuddin was answering a question from Pang Hok Liong (PH-Labis) regarding whether a Muslim foreign national who marries a Malaysian citizen of Malay ethnicity can be considered a Bumiputera.
Pang also asked whether they are eligible or not to enjoy the rights or privileges granted to Bumiputeras, as well as the conditions that must be met to obtain such eligibility.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NZ First's culture war push hits wall
Article:
Winston Peters, the veteran leader of New Zealand First, has borrowed heavily from the culture-war playbook that has energised populist parties across the English-speaking world, railing against "woke" politics, gender policy and high immigration ahead of next month's general election.
So far, political analysts say, the pay-off has been limited.
While the right has surged in countries such as Britain and Australia and Donald Trump's "Make America Great Again" (MAGA) platform secured him a second presidential term, Peters' decades-old New Zealand First remains a smaller force, even as it sharpens its message ahead of the country's Nov 7 vote.
Peters is betting that frustration over immigration, cost-of-living pressures and debates over national identity, gender and abortion can push his party to a stronger result and make it indispensable to Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's centre-right bloc.
But some analysts say the same rhetoric that has resonated abroad is running into a more secular, less polarised electorate at home.
Given current tight polling and New Zealand's proportional representation voting system, Luxon's National Party will need the seats of New Zealand First and the right-wing ACT party for a chance to form the government again and keep the country on its conservative track.
"This time it's almost now or never in terms of getting far greater power to implement our alternative to how to run an economy,"  said Peters, 81,  arguing voters had previously given New Zealand First only limited power.
Grant Welman, who runs a handyman business, said the crowd at a Peters event in Tauranga was made up of "everyday Kiwis" with "a deep concern for the direction of the country".
"I am voting New Zealand First this election, not because I believe they're the greatest, but I do believe that they are the best choice available."
Founded in 1993, New Zealand First has long combined social conservatism on issues such as immigration and Indigenous rights, with an interventionist economic programme that includes stronger state support for the elderly and regional development.
Peters has played a pivotal role in coalition-building, helping form four of the past 10 governments and serving as foreign minister in three.
This time around, he has ruled out a coalition with the centre-left Labour Party.
But Peters faces a new challenger to his role as kingmaker with the emergence of the centrist Opportunity party, which could hold the balance of power after the election.
It supports immigration, policies on LGBT rights and enhanced environmental protections.
Peters — who rejects the populist label, saying all politicians want to be popular — has framed his attacks on "woke" politics as a defence of common sense, experience and national sovereignty.
New Zealand First has sponsored a bill to define "woman" and "man" in law, has proposed immigration curbs and advocates leaving the Paris climate accord.
"The 2026 campaign is the most explicitly right-wing pitch NZ First has made in its 33-year history," said Josh Van Veen, a politics academic and former New Zealand First staffer.
"This might well be inspired by a global populist movement, but the polling would suggest it doesn't have quite the same appeal it does elsewhere in the Anglosphere."
New Zealand First won 6.1 per cent of the vote in 2023 and rose as high as 13.6 per cent in an April poll.
But recent surveys suggest that momentum has faded, putting the party's support around 10 per cent.
By contrast, Pauline Hanson's One Nation is nudging 30 per cent support in Australia, while Reform UK is at about 23.4 per cent in British polling averages.
"There just isn't a big constituency for the kind of MAGA-style politics that Peters and (NZ First lawmaker Shane) Jones sometimes lean into," said Van Veen, pointing to a recent 29-country survey that found New Zealanders the most open to immigration.
Ben Thomas, a political commentator, said  New Zealand was somewhat insulated from the culture wars because its proportional voting system did provide a "release valve for those views" and stopped them infiltrating the major parties as has been the case in the United States.
"It would be nice to think about New Zealanders as sort of rough-hewn, earthy common sense, which leaves them somewhat inoculated from those kind of global forces," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NST Leader: Cable thefts pose a grave national threat
Article:
MALAYSIAN public spaces and homes are so laden with prized assets and objects that they constantly attract thieves who steal and fence valuables with ease.
Besides targeting cars and motorcycles to strip for components, thieves burglarise homes for cash, jewellery, electrical and electronic appliances like laptops and smartphones. That's not all.
They also steal durian — the expensive musang king variety especially — from unprotected orchards, and rustle cattle ahead of major festive seasons when demand for meat spikes.
Years ago, thieves favoured steel manhole covers and brass water meters from residential homes.
The authorities have since switched to non-recyclable composite material with zero scrap value. Now, thieves target public utility and industrial cables, made valuable by surging copper and metal prices.
Top targets: telecom and rail copper cables, reflected by the recent Express Rail Link (ERL) airport corridor and national Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) cable thefts.
Thieves brazenly infiltrate substations and restricted rail lines to steal copper busbars and drain transformer oil that are illegally processed and resold as industrial lubricant.
Once petty thieves, they have morphed into organised syndicates, systematically siphoning public property and reselling them by the kilo.
Fenceable items must possess intrinsic value, no traceable serial numbers and an eager black market: easy to hide or transport, cut, unbolt or carry, and available in unsecured or predictable locations that yield high cash-per-kilo or cash-per-unit.
High demand is a given, but this is critical: stolen items are linked to a nefarious network of buyers — operators of unregulated scrap yards, rogue pawnshops or online buyers.
The recent cable thefts at the ERL track network and the Salak Tinggi station may net thieves between RM6,500 and RM13,000 —a day's work capitalising on high global copper prices.
To stop the thieves, authorities must stymie the rogues' ability to operate and their supply chain. Once indicted, penalties must include imprisonment and heavy fines.
In the long term, the best deterrent is to choke their market by inspecting and revoking licences of unscrupulous scrap disposal factories and illegal scrap metal dealers.
These dealers must digitally log all copper sales, to be cross-referenced against public utility logs for missing cables. Also go after every conceivable fence.
Prasarana and Malaysia Rail Link have shifted to intelligent CCTV using artificial intelligence to trigger alerts, marking cables with invisible trace-element liquid and embedding micro-trackers.
Repeated thefts of critical infrastructure seriously threaten public safety, essential services and economic activity. Define the thefts as a national security threat marshalled by relevant pre-emptive laws.
The priority is implementation, backed by clear responsibilities, coordinated intelligence-sharing and measurable enforcement results.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Government settles RM17.15bil in excess tax refunds as at Sept 30
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government has settled RM17.15 billion in excess tax refunds involving 3.23 million taxpayer cases as at Sept 30, 2026.
In a written reply published on Parliament's website today, the Finance Ministry said RM6.38 billion had been refunded to 3.1 million individual taxpayers, while RM8.95 billion went to more than 130,000 corporate taxpayers, including micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).
The ministry said the Inland Revenue Board had implemented measures to improve tax refund processing, including allocating refunds based on the age of outstanding cases and prioritising MSMEs and companies facing cash flow difficulties.
"The government is also committed to ensuring that outstanding refunds are fully settled promptly as part of efforts to enhance tax administration efficiency and safeguard taxpayers' rights, in line with the Madani government's fiscal reform agenda," it said.
The ministry was responding to a question from Lim Guan Eng (Bagan-PH) on the timeframe for settling excess tax refunds and the two per cent compensation for corporate taxpayers for the 2025 year of assessment.
He also sought details on outstanding refunds by year of assessment and the number of affected taxpayers.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Salam submarine cable project to begin in 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Madani Submarine Cable Connection (Salam) is expected to begin in the first quarter of 2027 and be completed by the fourth quarter of 2029, the Dewan Rakyat was told today.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) had issued an invitation for the project and was evaluating it. The implementing party is expected to be appointed by the fourth quarter of 2026.
The project aims to strengthen communications connectivity between Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak.
"It involves developing a high-capacity domestic submarine cable system with diverse network routes and backup capabilities to strengthen the resilience of the country's communications infrastructure," he said in a written parliamentary reply.
Meanwhile, Phase Two of the Jendela (National Digital Network) project is expected to begin in November, covering 1,000 sites nationwide, including 352 in Sabah.
Fahmi said internet coverage at the sites would be expanded through 4G cellular services, a combination of 4G and 5G, or satellite broadband, depending on local conditions and needs.
Kinabatangan accounts for the largest share of the 352 sites in Sabah, with 106, followed by Pensiangan with 55, Kota Marudu with 36, Kalabakan with 29 and Kudat with 26.
The remaining sites are in Tuaran (23), Penampang and Ranau (15 each), Sipitang (13), Kimanis (12), Sepanggar (six), Papar (five), Batu Sapi (four), Beaufort and Tawau (three each), and Putatan (one).
"The government, through MCMC, would continue to assess needs in other areas of Sabah, including Putatan, for possible expansion, subject to priorities and funding availability," he said.
The RM5 billion Jendela project aims to improve internet connectivity and bridge the digital divide, including in rural and remote areas and Orang Asli villages. It also targets connectivity along 7,000km of roads and highways and 1,700km of rail routes nationwide.
Fahmi was responding to a question from Datuk Shahelmey Yahya (BN-Putatan) on the status of Salam in Sabah and areas identified for Jendela Phase Two.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Whirlwind videos showing cars lifted into air go viral
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A car was seen being lifted into the air and thrown into another vehicle near the Damansara Toll Plaza during a thunderstorm, in footage that has gone viral on social media.
The video, posted on Threads by user @zhaeim, showed a
blue Perodua Alza
briefly lifted into the air before crashing into a white Perodua Ativa in the adjacent lane.
Another car farther ahead appeared to hover briefly as the whirlwind moved back and forth before dissipating during the thunderstorm.
The user said in a comment that the video belonged to a friend who was travelling home from work.
In a separate clip, Threads user @amnmnf_ showed a
whirlwind passing through the car park
of an apartment block in Kota Damansara, moving a red Perodua Axia several metres and making tall trees sway violently.
"Thunderstorm in the Kota Damansara area, oh God, the whirlwind is scary. Be careful to those riding home from work," the user wrote.
The videos drew shocked reactions from social media users. One said it was their first time seeing a "baby" whirlwind, while another wondered what might have happened if a motorcyclist or pedestrian had been passing by.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Squishy toy raid: Over 2,300 uncertified toys seized without MC mark
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: The Terengganu Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry has seized 2,380 squishy toys worth RM30,391 over suspected non-compliance with safety standards since Oct 3.
Its director, Mohd Mufsi Lat, said the soft, sponge-like toys, which came in various shapes and designs, were seized following 101 inspections across the state.
He said the inspections found that the toys allegedly did not carry the Malaysian conformity (MC) mark, as required under the relevant regulations.
"Action was taken against six premises in Kuala Terengganu, with investigations opened under the Consumer Protection Act 1999 and regulations governing toy safety standards.
"Toys designed or intended for use in play by children under 14 must comply with the prescribed safety standards," he said in a statement today.
Mufsi said companies found guilty could be fined up to RM250,000 for a first offence, while individuals could face a fine of up to RM100,000, jail for up to three years, or both.

Title: Sabah schools to close if API exceeds 150 for three consecutive days
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Schools in Sabah will be temporarily closed if the Air Pollutant Index (API) exceeds 150 for three consecutive days, the state government has announced.
State Secretary Datuk Zainudin Aman, who is also State Disaster Management Committee chairman, said the measure was taken to protect pupils and teachers from the adverse health effects of haze.
"This measure is also in line with the Education Ministry's directive following the advice of Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim," he said in a statement today.
As of 7pm, Tawau was the only district to record an API reading above the threshold, at 155.
All schools in Tawau have been ordered to close from tomorrow amid worsening haze conditions.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar expresses 'utter disgust' over international community's failure on Palestine
Article:
BANGI: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has expressed deep disappointment over the international order's failure to address the Palestinian cause, describing it as a failure to uphold democracy and human rights.
Anwar questioned the consistency of the international community in upholding these principles, saying Palestinians should not be subjected to different standards of treatment.
"What is so hypocritical is the failure of the international community. I have to speak as the prime minister, and I understand that.
"But I have to express my utter disgust with the failure of the international order. What order is there without democracy and human rights, when human beings are treated like animals and slaves?" he said in his speech at the Sumud Nusantara Dinner today.
The dinner was held in conjunction with the Global Sumud Congress 2026.
Also present were Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, Youth and Sports Minister Dr Taufiq Johari, Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Senator Dr Zulkifli Hasan, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari and Sumud Nusantara Command Centre director-general Datuk Dr Ahmad Sani Araby.
Anwar said generations in formerly colonised countries had fought colonialism and imperialism because they opposed injustice, oppression and colonisation.
"Now, we are in a society that condones the very same principles we fought against for decades under colonialism and imperialism," he said.
Citing Gaza, Anwar said the suffering of Palestinians should not be viewed as a recent development, but understood in the context of decades of oppression.
"Some say it has only happened in the past few years, but those who understand history know that this oppression has continued for 70 years.
"What is the problem? Is it because they are the Arabs, Palestinians and Muslims? There is no answer.
"Why is it that, when it comes to the Palestinian cause, there is a different set of arrangements, judgments and decisions?" he said.
Anwar added that he had raised the issue with counterparts in Europe, the United States and elsewhere, questioning whether Palestinians were being treated differently because of their religious or ethnic identities.
"To me, it does not matter. What is important is that they are human beings, and they cannot be colonised," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trailer driver killed in Batu Pahat crash
Article:
BATU PAHAT: A trailer driver was killed after his vehicle rear-ended a lorry on the North-South Expressway near Ayer Hitam.
Ayer Hitam Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Abd Rahim Razali said the 56-year-old man was confirmed dead at the scene by a medical team.
The accident occurred at 3.50pm at KM93.5 of the northbound North-South Expressway. The trailer was carrying wooden pallets, while the lorry was transporting a skylift.
Abd Rahim said the trailer hit the rear of the lorry, causing the wooden pallets to crush the trailer's cab and trapping the driver.
The lorry driver and his assistant, both in their 40s, survived.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MRR2 flyover accident: Soldier dies after falling onto motorcyclist near TBS
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: An Armed Forces personnel was killed after falling about 5m from a flyover onto another motorcyclist on the Middle Ring Road 2 (MRR2) near Terminal Bersepadu Selatan (TBS) this morning.
Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief assistant commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the incident occurred at 8.04am as the 24-year-old soldier was travelling from his home in Bukit Jalil to his workplace at Sungai Besi Camp.
He said the soldier, who was riding a Honda Wave motorcycle, was believed to have lost control while negotiating a ramp on the flyover near TBS to make a U-turn.
The soldier was thrown onto the road below, while his motorcycle remained on the flyover.
"The victim landed on a 46-year-old man riding a Honda Vario motorcycle from Cheras towards Sungai Besi, causing both to fall onto the road.
"At the same time, a lorry driven by a 46-year-old man tried to avoid the two victims but failed and hit the Honda Vario motorcycle," he said in a statement today.
Zamzuri said the soldier sustained severe head and bodily injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene.
The Honda Vario rider suffered a fractured left arm, facial injuries and internal head bleeding. He was taken to Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz for treatment.
The lorry driver escaped unharmed.
Mohd Zamzuri said the case was being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
He urged members of the public or witnesses with information to contact the Tun H.S. Lee Traffic Police Station at 03-2071 9999 or any nearby police station to assist in the investigation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Govt urged to clarify police body camera rollout
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government has been urged to explain the status of the nationwide rollout of police body cameras.
Kepong member of parliament Lim Lip Eng said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail had informed him in a parliamentary reply in October 2023 that the cameras were expected to be fully deployed by the first quarter of 2025.
In June 2025, it was reported that 7,648 police personnel had been equipped with body cameras under a phased rollout that began in October 2024, with another 10,000 units planned under the 13th Malaysia Plan.
Lim also urged police to ensure that all searches had a clear legal basis.
He proposed allowing the offices of elected representatives to observe enforcement raids to improve transparency.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lorry driver in 12-vehicle crash released on bail
Article:
SHAH ALAM: A 51-year-old lorry driver charged over a 12-vehicle crash that injured four people last Friday has been released on bail after paying a total of RM12,900.
His lawyer, Rohan Singh, said the bail was settled through two sureties after proceedings in two separate courts concluded this afternoon.
However, he said he was unsure who had acted as the bailors.
The courts set bail at RM9,000 with one surety for the charge of driving under the influence of drugs and RM3,900 with one surety for the drug consumption charge.
Earlier, C.
Agilan pleaded not guilty
to both charges in separate magistrates' courts.
On the first charge, Agilan was accused of driving a lorry under the influence of methamphetamine and amphetamine, causing him to lose control of the vehicle and injure four people aged between 17 and 58.
The incident occurred about 4.30pm along Persiaran Mokhtar Dahari, where the 10-tonne lorry allegedly travelled against the flow of traffic before crashing into 11 vehicles at the Alam Budiman traffic lights.
The charge was framed under Section 44(1A)(a) of the Road Transport Act 1987, which carries a maximum jail term of 10 years and a fine of up to RM50,000 upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Alia Anisa Khairus Masnan sought bail of RM15,000 and requested that Agilan's driving licence be suspended.
Rohan sought a lower amount, telling the court that his client earned about RM1,700 a month and supported his non-working wife and 11-year-old child.

Title: Fitch: Malaysia's 2027 Budget deficit target hinges on revenue, subsidies
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's plan to narrow its fiscal deficit to 3.3 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 2027 faces pressure from elevated subsidy costs and social spending, Fitch Ratings said.
The target compares with a revised deficit of 3.6 per cent for 2026 and maintains the government's medium-term fiscal consolidation path, although spending pressures could limit the pace of improvement.
The 2026 deficit target was initially set at 3.5 per cent of GDP, but higher subsidy costs pushed revised expenditure nearly six per cent above the original budget.
Total expenditure in 2027 is projected to increase 3.6 per cent from the revised 2026 base, while development expenditure is budgeted to rise 2.5 per cent.
Under the 2027-2029 Medium-Term Fiscal Framework (MTFF), the government targets an average fiscal deficit of 3.1 per cent of GDP, compared with 3.2 per cent under the previous 2026-2028 framework.
Fitch said achieving the targets would depend on revenue collection and more efficient subsidy mechanisms.
This could become more challenging if oil prices remain elevated or social spending pressures persist ahead of the election.
The MTFF assumes average real GDP growth of five per cent, at the upper end of the government's 2027 growth forecast of 4.2 to 5.2 per cent and above Fitch's projection of 4.5 per cent.
Subsidies and social assistance will remain a major fiscal constraint, with allocations budgeted at RM72.7 billion, or about 3.1 per cent of GDP, in 2027.
This follows a nearly 35 per cent upward revision in the allocation to RM74.5 billion for 2026.
Fitch said the government has retained petroleum price caps and introduced a similar mechanism for diesel from July 2026, alongside additional household and business support, including higher cash assistance and tax reductions.
Revenue is projected to grow 4.7 per cent in 2027, supported by economic expansion, stronger tax collection and compliance, and contributions from government-linked entities.
These include RM32 billion from Petroliam Nasional Bhd, RM3 billion from sovereign wealth fund Khazanah Nasional Bhd and RM7 billion from Bank Negara Malaysia.
Stronger-than-expected revenue collection in 2026 has partly offset the higher subsidy bill, Fitch said.
Government debt is expected to continue declining gradually, supported by nominal GDP growth and the planned reduction in the fiscal deficit.
Fitch expects debt to fall to about 74 per cent of GDP in 2027 from 77.3 per cent in 2025.
However, the projected level remains substantially above the 'BBB' rating category median of 57.4 per cent.
Its debt measure includes committed guarantees, estimated at 11.4 per cent of GDP in 2026.
Fitch said a sustained reduction in government debt relative to GDP towards peer medians, supported by fiscal consolidation or stronger growth prospects, could put upward pressure on Malaysia's 'BBB+' sovereign rating, which carries a Stable Outlook.

Title: Former Perak Immigration prosecution chief to begin three-year jail term for corruption
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: A former Perak Immigration Department Prosecution Unit chief began serving a three-year prison sentence today after the Court of Appeal reinstated his conviction for soliciting and accepting bribes 11 years ago.
A three-member panel led by Judge Datuk Noorin Badaruddin, in an unanimous decision, allowed the prosecution's final appeal to set aside the Ipoh High Court's decision that had acquitted Zaidi Dali, 58.
Noorin, presiding alongside Judges Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid and Datuk Seri Mohd Radzi Harun, stated in her judgment that the High Court judge erred in acquitting Zaidi.
She said the prosecution had presented sufficient grounds to enable the court to intervene in the appeal.
"Therefore, we are satisfied that the prosecution's case, when evaluated based on the correct legal principles and as a whole, has proven the charge against the respondent beyond a reasonable doubt," she said.
"The conviction recorded by the Sessions Court judge is reinstated. We also find no basis to disturb the sentence imposed by the otherworldly Sessions Court.
"Therefore, the sentence is also reinstated," she said, while ordering a committal warrant to be issued immediately.
She said after examining the overall evidence, the court was satisfied that the evidence regarding the meeting between PW3 (Prosecution Witness 3) and Zaidi, as well as subsequent events, supported the findings of the Sessions Court judge.
"The allegation of a 'request' must be evaluated as part of the entire incident and not as an isolated conversation separated from the events before and after it," she said.
Regarding the acceptance of the RM7,000, Noorin said there was a chain of evidence concerning the receipt of the RM7,000 based on the testimonies of prosecution witnesses.
Noorin said corruption can erode public confidence, and therefore public authorities accused of abusing their positions for personal gain must take such accusations seriously.
The prosecution appealed against the Ipoh High Court's decision on August 8, 2025, which had acquitted Zaidi of both charges.
On September 23, 2022, the Ipoh Sessions Court sentenced Zaidi to three years in prison and a fine of RM85,000 after finding him guilty of soliciting and accepting bribes.
Zaidi, in his capacity as the Perak Immigration Department Prosecution Unit chief was charged with soliciting a bribe of RM10,000 per month from Nga Chee Jiek as an inducement to ensure that no inspections and raids were conducted at an entertainment center in Pusat Bandar Seri Manjung.
The offence was committed at the Meru Valley Golf & Country Club at 9:00 pm on November 5, 2015, under Section 16(a)(B) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act 2009.
He was also charged with obtaining a bribe of RM7,000 from Nga for himself as an inducement to ensure no inspections and raids were conducted on the same entertainment center at the parking lot of the Meru Valley Golf & Country Club at 9:55 pm on November 11, 2015, under Section 17(a) of the MACC Act 2009.
During today's proceedings, the prosecution was represented by Deputy Public Prosecutor Farah Ezlin Yusop Khan, while Zaidi was represented by lawyer Datuk M. Athimulan.

Title: Haze expected to ease over next two weeks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The transboundary haze that has affected Malaysia's air quality since Aug 8 is expected to gradually subside over the next two weeks as wind patterns change, Deputy Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Syed Ibrahim Syed Noh said.
He said Malaysia entered the monsoon transition phase on Oct 9, with the northeast monsoon expected to begin towards the end of this month.
"However, I want to emphasise that changes in weather conditions alone are not a long-term solution to the haze issue. It could happen again.
"Fire prevention efforts must therefore address the problem at its source. Domestic enforcement must be strengthened, while regional cooperation must be enhanced to reduce the risk of similar incidents recurring," he said during the Special Chamber session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Syed Ibrahim was responding to concerns raised by Khoo Poay Tiong (PH-Kota Melaka), who described the haze as a national crisis affecting public health, safety, the economy and public well-being.
The issue was also raised by Dr Kelvin Yii Lee Wuen (PH-Bandar Kuching) and Young Syefura Othman (PH-Bentong).
Yii said the haze was no longer merely a seasonal nuisance but an annual emergency requiring stronger action, including a proposed Cross-Border Haze Pollution Act and greater transparency in sharing hotspot data and information on plantation concessions.
Young Syefura sought clarification on the government's diplomatic engagements with Indonesia, including the responses received and the effectiveness of measures taken.
She also called for stronger domestic enforcement and better protection for vulnerable groups.
Syed Ibrahim said the latest haze episode was caused by an increase in forest and land fires in several parts of Indonesia, including Kalimantan and Sumatra, which had affected air quality in Malaysia, particularly in Sarawak.
He said the Department of Environment (DOE) received 2,104 complaints concerning open burning and carried out 3,039 enforcement actions between Aug 3 and Oct 9.
These comprised 2,104 monitoring actions, 168 field orders, 32 notices, 13 compounds and two court actions.
As part of mitigation efforts, the government also conducted 11 cloud-seeding operations between Aug 30 and Oct 15 in collaboration with the Malaysian Meteorological Department and the National Disaster Management Agency.
"The main challenge in enforcing laws with cross-border elements is obtaining sufficient evidence to establish the source of pollution and identify the parties responsible," he said.
Syed Ibrahim added that the ministry had yet to receive official information from the Foreign Affairs Ministry or the Plantation and Commodities Ministry regarding the alleged involvement of Malaysian companies in open-burning incidents in Indonesia.

Title: [UPDATED] Man arrested in Indonesia with 4kg syabu is not Malaysian student
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police have dismissed viral social media claims that a Malaysian university student was arrested in Indonesia for attempting to smuggle 4kg of methamphetamine, commonly known as syabu, into the country.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said investigations confirmed that the suspect arrested by Indonesian authorities was Indonesian, not Malaysian as claimed in circulating reports.
He said the man was detained by Tanjung Balai police in North Sumatra on Oct 10 after arriving at Teluk Nibung Ferry Terminal from Port Dickson, Negri Sembilan.
"Preliminary investigations found that Indonesian authorities detained an Indonesian man who had arrived at the Teluk Nibung Ferry Terminal from Port Dickson.
"An inspection of his belongings uncovered eight plastic packages containing substances suspected to be methamphetamine, weighing approximately 4kg," he said in a statement today.
Hussein said further investigations revealed that the drugs had been handed to the suspect by another Indonesian man in the Klang Valley.
The suspect was believed to have been tasked with transporting the drugs into Indonesia through the Tanjung Balai ferry terminal.
He said police had taken note of social media reports claiming that a Malaysian university student had been caught smuggling the drugs.
However, he stressed that the claims were inaccurate and could cause unnecessary confusion and concern among Malaysians.
"The claim that a Malaysian was arrested and that a university student was caught smuggling 4kg of syabu is untrue.
"Such inaccurate information can create confusion and anxiety among members of the public," he said.
Hussein urged media organisations and the public to verify information with the relevant authorities before publishing or sharing reports, particularly those involving international drug trafficking cases.
He said the NCID would continue working closely with Indonesian authorities to gather intelligence and establish the source of the drugs.
Investigators would also seek to dismantle the drug trafficking network operating in Malaysia believed to be linked to the case.
He urged anyone with information on drug trafficking activities to contact the NCID hotline at 012-208 7222.

Title: [UPDATED] Ex-pilot with drug record, foreign woman identified in Laos private jet drug probe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian police have identified two Filipinos, including a former pilot, believed to be linked to an international drug trafficking syndicate behind the seizure of 521kg of methamphetamine from a private jet in Laos.
Federal Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the former pilot had chartered the aircraft through a Malaysian broker, while the woman was believed to have acted as the syndicate's coordinator.
The former pilot, 54, has a drug-related criminal record in the Philippines, while the woman is 51.
Hussein said the latest findings followed investigations into the seizure at
Luang Prabang International Airport on Oct 1,
which also led to the detention of a Malaysian second officer.
"Investigations have identified the syndicate and individuals in Malaysia who are believed to be connected to the case.
"So far, the NCID has recorded statements from several witnesses, including a local who acted as a broker in arranging the charter of the aircraft.
"The individual revealed that the aircraft was chartered by a 54-year-old Filipino man who was identified as a former pilot with a drug-related criminal record in the Philippines," he said in a statement.
The NCID's Special Investigation Unit is investigating the case under Sections 34 and 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952. Section 34 covers conspiracy or preparatory acts in Malaysia for drug trafficking offences committed overseas.
Hussein said Malaysian investigators were working with the Foreign Ministry and the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA) to obtain further information, establish the involvement of those linked to the syndicate and identify others who may have facilitated the operation.
Lao authorities seized about 521kg of crystal methamphetamine from the private jet at Luang Prabang International Airport on Oct 1 and detained 13 people, including a Malaysian second officer.
Malaysian investigations found that the aircraft had departed Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport in Subang for Luang Prabang without cargo.
The jet was believed to have been chartered to transport the drugs from Laos to Manila, the Philippines.
At a press conference on Oct 9, Hussein said the aircraft had been
chartered for US$49,500
(about RM209,000) to transport a shipment declared as goods from Laos to the Philippines.
He said investigators believed the person who arranged the charter was a Filipino national, whose details had been shared with Philippine authorities to help trace and apprehend those responsible.
Malaysian police had also arrested a 49-year-old Malaysian pilot who owned an aviation company linked to the jet.
The drugs were declared as vape products in the aircraft's cargo manifest to conceal the shipment bound for Manila.
Hussein said the NCID remained committed to combating drug trafficking syndicates through cooperation with international enforcement agencies.

Title: Police: Two investigation papers opened over RM350,000 bribery claim against senior MACC officer
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 13 — Two separate investigation papers have been opened into allegations that a senior Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) officer received a bribe of RM350,000 from an individual in 2017.
Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M. Kumar said the investigations were initiated following a police report lodged over the matter, which had gone viral on several social media platforms.
He said the first investigation paper was opened under Section 165 of the Penal Code, which deals with public servants accepting valuable items without consideration from persons connected to their official duties.
“If convicted, offenders face imprisonment for up to two years, a fine, or both,” he said in a statement today.
Kumar said the investigation is being conducted under Section 500 of the Penal Code for defamation, which carries a maximum penalty of two years’ jail, a fine, or both upon conviction.
He said police are also investigating possible offences under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 for the improper use of network facilities or services and carries a fine of up to RM500,000, imprisonment of up to two years, or both, upon conviction.
Kumar said police would also submit an application for an Order to Investigate under Section 108(2) of the Criminal Procedure Code to the Public Prosecutor to facilitate further investigations.
“This includes recording witness statements and obtaining confirmation of the status of previous investigations conducted by the MACC,” he said.
He urged the public not to speculate on the case and advised them to use social media responsibly to safeguard the country’s peace and security.
On Saturday (October 10), Malaysian Corruption Watch (MCW) urged the MACC and the Anti-Corruption Advisory Board (ACAB) to promptly investigate the allegations involving the senior officer to safeguard the agency’s integrity.

Title: Home Ministry to seek details on five Malaysians held in Japan drug bust, says Saifuddin Nasution
Article:
